newsitem.title: USA: NY securitization seen allowing 5.5 pct rate cut.
newsitem.headline: NY securitization seen allowing 5.5 pct rate cut.

text.p: The New York State Consumer Protection Board has estimated that securitization of stranded costs would allow New York electric utilities to reduce rates by $780.4 million per year, or 5.5 percent.

If the full amount were flowed through to residential, small business and farm customers, rates in these categories could be reduced by 10 to 11 percent, the board said in testimony Wednesday to the state Senate Energy Committee.
The potential savings range from 1.9 percent for Long Island Lighting Co to 7.7 percent for New York State Electric & Gas Corp, the board estimates.

Both Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc and Niagara Mohawk Power Corp are seen with potential rate cuts of 6.3 percent, while Central Hudson Gas & Electric Corp has the potential to reduce rates by 3.9 percent, Orange and Rockland Utilities Inc by 3.8 percent and Rochester Gas & Electric Corp by 2.9 percent.
Of the total rate reduction, the board attributed $388.0 million a year to reduced IPP costs.
The staff of the Public Service Commission told the hearing it estimates savings from securitization on IPP contracts would be $387 million in the first year.

With the first year being 1997, the commission's staff estimated the savings would drop to $14 million a year in 2016 with a levelized annual savings of $248 million. The 20 year savings would total $3.76 billion -- an amount having a net present value of $2.11 billion, the staff testimony said.

It put the net present value of securitizing regulatory assets at $3.81 billion and intangible assets at $3.04 billion, saying these two areas together would result in savings of $91 million in each of the 20 years.
The testimony reiterated the chairman's goal of reducing rates to large commercial and industrial customers by 25 percent.

The Consumer Protection Board estimates the lower interest rates resulting from securitization would let Niagara Mohawk cut its cost of capital by 46.5 percent while Lilco's would go down only 7.2 percent. In between are Rochester G&E, at 14.6 percent; Central Hudson, at 24.8 percent; Orange & Rockland, at 29.3 percent; and Con Edison, at 38.5 percent.

The agency estimated stranded costs for the companies at $376.0 million, or 28.9 percent of total assets, for Central Hudson; $7.57 billion, or 52.9 percent of assets, for Con Edison; and 384.0 million, or 31.9 percent of assets, for Orange & Rockland.

Also, $4.06 billion, or 77.7 percent of assets, for NYSEG, $2.03 billion, or 81.6 percent of assets, for Rochester G&E, $7.52 billion, or 57.6 percent of assets, for Lilco; and 4.22 billion, or 41.5 percent of assets, for Niagara Mohawk.

It said Moody's put the stranded estimates at $231 million for Central Hudson, $3.9 billion for Con Edison, 227 million for Orange & Rockland, $1.9 billion for NYSEG, $605 million for Rochester G&E, $6.9 billion for Lilco and $5.0 billion for Niagara Mohawk.
The estimate for Niagara Mohawk's own estimate was close to the company's own estimate, which put the portion for IPP contracts at $4.7 billion.

The board's testimony did not include Niagara Mohawk's own estimate, but it did say Con Edison estimates its stranded assets at $4.7 billion, Orange & Rockland puts its at $43 million and NYSEG has released a $2.3 billion estimate.

The board estimated assets that could be securitized under the pending legislation at $287.0 million, or 22.1 percent of total assets, for Central Hudson; $2.36 billion, or 16.5 percent of assets, for Con Edison; $221.0 million, or 18.3 percent of assets, for Orange & Rockland; $1.25 billion, or 23.9 percent of assets, for NYSEG; $482.0 million, or 19.4 percent of assets, for Rochester G&E; $2.29 billion, or 17.6 percent of assets for Lilco; and $716.0 million, or 7.1 percent of assets, for Niagara Mohawk.
For the three utilities with the highest IPP costs, the board estimated securitization savings of $124.5 million a year for Con Edison, $63.9 million for NYSEG and $199.5 million for Niagara Mohawk.

It put their present costs at $900.0 million, $297.0 million and $979.9 million, respectively, and the present value of the above market costs to be securitized at $3.0 billion, R956.3 million and $2.5 billion.
